findings.evidence: "Request or approval: name the smallest decision, who owns it, and the needed-by time." The workflow also says "Status or FYI: say what changes for the recipient and whether any response is needed." Much of the workflow activates familiar professional-writing practices rather than supplying expert-only knowledge.
findings.fix: Condense the routine request/status guidance into one rule: "Lead with the decision or recipient impact; include the context needed to act, and do not invent an ask for an FYI." Retain the more distinctive scope trade-offs, missing-thread fallback, uncertainty preservation and proposed-deadline safeguards.

findings.evidence: "NEVER paste internal logs, incident links or stack traces into a message to external or wider recipients without checking disclosure and that they can open them" has no unresolved-disclosure branch. Step 1 says "Ask only for blocking gaps" after defining the blocking gap as no topic and no source draft, while step 4 requires "every source fact kept". An external rewrite containing sensitive source details can therefore require clarification or redaction that the workflow does not explicitly permit.
findings.fix: Add a disclosure fallback before drafting: when permission or recipient access is unknown, omit internal links and sensitive details, use a safe summary or an explicit placeholder, and identify anything withheld. Treat disclosure confirmation as a blocking question when a safe draft is impossible, and exempt deliberate redactions from the every-source-fact validation rule.
